keys.denied.description: First-run setup configures instance-wide defaults, so it can only be run by an operator of the system tenant. Sign in with the operator account to continue.
keys.denied.title: Setup is operator-only
keys.finish.defaults: Setup complete. You can fine-tune everything in Settings.
keys.finish.saved: Setup complete. Your instance is ready.
keys.guide.email.connection.from: From address / name is what recipients see the mail come from.
keys.guide.email.connection.heading: SMTP connection
keys.guide.email.connection.host: Host — your provider’s SMTP server, e.g. mail.yourdomain.com (cPanel), smtp.gmail.com (Google), or email-smtp.<region>.amazonaws.com (Amazon SES).
keys.guide.email.connection.port: Port + Encryption go together: 587 → TLS (STARTTLS) or 465 → SSL. Use a hostname the TLS certificate actually covers.
keys.guide.email.connection.username: Username is usually the full email address of the mailbox you send from.
keys.guide.email.credentials.cpanel: cPanel: Email Accounts → Connect Devices shows the host, ports and username.
keys.guide.email.credentials.google: Google Workspace / Gmail: create an App Password (with 2-Step Verification on) and use it as the SMTP password.
keys.guide.email.credentials.heading: Where to find your credentials
keys.guide.email.credentials.ses: Amazon SES: create SMTP credentials in the SES console (these are distinct from your AWS keys).
keys.guide.email.password.body: The SMTP password is stored encrypted and set on the Email settings page, which also has a “send test email” button to verify the connection end-to-end.
keys.guide.email.password.heading: Password & test send
keys.guide.email.summary: How to connect an SMTP mailbox — and where to find the details.
keys.guide.email.transport.heading: Transport
keys.guide.email.transport.options: “None” disables email entirely. “Log” writes messages to the app log (handy while testing). “SMTP” sends real email through your mail provider.
keys.guide.signin.masterSwitch: This is the instance-wide master switch for federated sign-in. When off, every configured identity provider is disabled.
keys.guide.signin.providers: Individual providers (e.g. Google) are added on the SSO settings page: create an OAuth client in your provider, set the redirect URI it gives you, then paste the client ID/secret there.
keys.guide.signin.summary: The SSO master switch; add individual providers on the SSO page.
keys.guide.signup.approval: Require admin approval holds each new account as “pending” until an administrator approves it. Leave it on when sign-up is open so nobody gets access unreviewed.
keys.guide.signup.publicSignup: Public sign-up lets anyone create an account from the sign-in screen. It is OFF by default — an operator-provisioned instance opens it deliberately.
keys.guide.signup.summary: What open sign-up and approval mean for your instance.
keys.guide.storage.driver.heading: Driver
keys.guide.storage.driver.local: “local” stores uploaded files on the server’s disk — fine for a single-node deployment.
keys.guide.storage.driver.s3: For durability or multi-node, use an S3-compatible object store (AWS S3, MinIO, Cloudflare R2, Backblaze B2, …) by setting the driver to “s3”.
keys.guide.storage.s3.accessKey: Access key — the public key ID. The matching SECRET key is supplied via the deployment environment and is never stored here.
keys.guide.storage.s3.endpoint: Endpoint — the object store’s base URL (e.g. https://s3.amazonaws.com, or your MinIO/R2 endpoint).
keys.guide.storage.s3.heading: S3 settings
keys.guide.storage.s3.pathStyle: Path-style addressing — turn on for most self-hosted gateways (MinIO); AWS uses virtual-hosted style.
keys.guide.storage.s3.publicBaseUrl: Public base URL — set only if assets are served from a different (CDN) host than the endpoint.
keys.guide.storage.s3.region: Region / Bucket — as created in your provider’s console.
keys.guide.storage.summary: Keep files on local disk, or point at an S3-compatible object store.
